caption: [Fire @ Blk 103B, Depot Road]Earlier today at about 5:30pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, black smoke was emitting from a twelve-floor unit.The fire, which involved one of the rooms within the unit, was extinguished with two water jets. caption: [Punggol Marine Fire Post Groundbreaking Ceremony]The groundbreaking ceremony for SCDFs new Punggol Marine Fire Post (PMFP) was held earlier today (16 Jan). Mr Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry, graced the event as the Guest of Honour.The integrated land-and-sea PMFP marks a significant milestone in strengthening SCDFs emergency response capabilities in the Northeast region of Singapore. Housing a suite of land and sea-based emergency assets, the PMFP will improve response time and strengthen land-based coverage for residents in Northshore, whilst extending marine-based coverage across the entire East Johor Straits within 45 minutes.Slated for completion in end 2027, the PMFP will address evolving emergency response needs as the Punggol region continues to undergo rapid development, with new residential precincts, transport infrastructure, major developments, and maritime activities in the East Johor Straits.In line with SCDFs commitment to environmental sustainability, the PMFP will also incorporate energy-efficient and water-saving features, including solar photovoltaic panels to reduce energy consumption, and water-efficient fittings and systems to minimise water usage. It has also been designed with community-friendly features to complement the recreational and lifestyle landscape of the Punggol Northshore district.Developed in close partnership with , part of , the PMFP will feature shared usage of jetty infrastructure and facilities to optimise the utilisation of land and sea space.With todays groundbreaking ceremony, this milestone underscores SCDFs continued commitment to strengthening both land and marine emergency response, contributing to a safer and more resilient community in the Northeast region of Singapore. caption: [34th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade]Earlier today, 41 officer cadets from the 34th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Amongst the graduating cohort were seven cadets from the Ministry of Interior, Kingdom of Bahrain and two cadets from the Vietnam Police Department of Fire & Rescue.These cadets have undergone a comprehensive seven-month training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations. As Senior Officers, they will lead their fellow officers to advance the lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property.In his speech, the guest of honour, Mr Goh Pei Ming, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development, encouraged the newly commissioned cadets to lead their teams with conviction and uphold high standards in their work, while carrying out their duties with pride and care.During the event, five Officer Cadets were presented with awards to recognise their achievements in the following categories:- Overall Best Trainee: OCT Muhamad Hail Aryyan Bin Muhamad Abdullah- Best in Practical: OCT Mohd Hafizz Bin Mohd Akebal- Best in Knowledge: OCT Phone Min Myat- Best in Physical Training: OCT Seth Kho Yao-En- Best Performing International Cadet: OCT Nguyen Chi CuongCongratulations to the 34th RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their lifesaving journey. ANationOfLifesavers

caption: [34th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade]Earlier today, 41 officer cadets from the 34th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Amongst the graduating cohort were seven cadets from the Ministry of Interior, Kingdom of Bahrain and two cadets from the Vietnam Police Department of Fire & Rescue.These cadets have undergone a comprehensive seven-month training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations. We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their lifesaving journey. ANationOfLifesavers

caption: [34th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade]Earlier today, 41 officer cadets from the 34th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Amongst the graduating cohort were seven cadets from the Ministry of Interior, Kingdom of Bahrain and two cadets from the Vietnam Police Department of Fire & Rescue.These cadets have undergone a comprehensive seven-month training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations. As Senior Officers, they will lead their fellow officers to advance the lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property.In his speech, the guest of honour, Mr Goh Pei Ming, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development, encouraged the newly commissioned cadets to lead their teams with conviction and uphold high standards in their work, while carrying out their duties with pride and care.During the event, five Officer Cadets were presented with awards to recognise their achievements in the following categories:- Overall Best Trainee: OCT Muhamad Hail Aryyan Bin Muhamad Abdullah- Best in Practical: OCT Mohd Hafizz Bin Mohd Akebal- Best in Knowledge: OCT Phone Min Myat- Best in Physical Training: OCT Seth Kho Yao-En- Best Performing International Cadet: OCT Nguyen Chi CuongCongratulations to the 34th RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their lifesaving journey. ANationOfLifesavers

caption: [Fire @ Block 29, Tampines Street 86]Earlier today (9 Jan) at about 9:05pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms inside a unit on the 15th floor was on fire. Firefighters conducted forcible entry into the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with two water jets. The fire was largely confined to the bedroom. No one was inside the unit at the time of the fire.About 100 persons from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.During the firefighting operation, a firefighter experienced heat exhaustion and was conveyed to Changi General Hospital. The cause of the fire is under investigation.Members of the public are advised to practise the following home fire safety habits to help prevent the most common causes of residential fires:-- Do not leave cooking unattended.- Do not overload power sockets; switch off electrical supply when not in use. - Extinguish lighted materials, such as candles, before leaving home.Update: The firefighter was discharged from CGH on the same day (9 Jan) and is feeling well.

caption: [SCDF Fire Safety Enforcement Blitz at Commercial Premises]As part of SCDFs ongoing efforts to maintain and enforce a high standard of fire safety in buildings and premises, an enforcement blitz was conducted last week.SCDF detected several fire safety non-compliances at two commercial premises. These include obstructions to exit doors, dry risers and fire extinguishers, non-maintenance of fire safety provisions such as hosereels and fire alarms, and improper storage of combustibles at one of the premises. Enforcement actions, such as the issuing of a Fire Hazard Abatement Notice (FHAN), will be taken against the responsible entities for the various non-compliances. A FHAN is a written warning requiring the responsible entities to take the necessary steps to abate the fire hazard within a specific time period, and prevent its recurrence.Premises owners are reminded to fully comply with fire safety regulations to ensure the safety of everyone.Remember, fire safety is a collective responsibility!

caption: [Fire Incident along Chiku Road]Earlier this morning at about 4:00am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, three single-storey terrace units (Unit no: 8, 10, 12) were on fire and spreading to the adjacent units. SCDF firefighters immediately set up water jets to surround and contain the fire to the three units. A Combined Platform Ladder was also deployed for aerial firefighting and prevent the further spread of the fire. At the height of the operation, a total of seven water jets were deployed.The fire was extinguished at about 6:45am. As a result of the fire, six adjoining terrace units (Unit no: 2, 4, 6, 14, 16 and 18) sustained varying degree of burn damage. Damping down* of the affected area is ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. About 20 persons from the affected units, as well as neighboring units were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.One person was assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. This is to prevent the rekindling of the fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

question_0: How does the response strategy of the Singapore Civil Defence Force during nighttime fire incidents ensure the safety of both the firefighters and the surrounding community?
answer_0: The response strategy of the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) during nighttime fire incidents is designed to ensure both firefighter safety and community security through several key measures. 

Firstly, the use of protective gear is crucial. In the image, firefighters are seen equipped with helmets and suits, which offer them enhanced protection against heat and smoke, reducing risks of injury. This is particularly important at night when visibility is compromised due to low light and thick smoke, as highlighted in the scene.

Additionally, the deployment of a Combined Platform Ladder for aerial firefighting allows responders to tackle the fire from above, effectively controlling it while minimizing exposure to direct flames for those on the ground. This strategy not only helps contain the fire but also safeguards firefighters against falling debris or intense heat.

The SCDF also emphasizes community safety by evacuating nearby residents, as indicated by the precautionary measures mentioned in the dialogue. By preemptively removing individuals from surrounding units, the SCDF minimizes the risk of injury or smoke inhalation. The treatment of one person for smoke inhalation at Singapore General Hospital further illustrates the importance placed on community health during such incidents.

Finally, damping down operations—aimed at ensuring no residual flames reignite—reflects a thorough and systematic approach to firefighting that prioritizes both immediate containment and long-term safety for the community. This comprehensive strategy integrates advanced firefighting techniques, protective equipment, and community health considerations, especially relevant during challenging nighttime scenarios.

caption: [Rescue Incident @ Block 338A Tah Ching Road]Earlier today (27 Nov) at about 1:35pm, SCDF received a call for assistance at the abovementioned location.Firefighters from Jurong Fire Station and rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team responded to this incident.Upon SCDFs arrival, a person was found in a unit with his entire left arm trapped in a drain pipe under the kitchen sink. The rescue operation involved a team of rescuers removing the kitchen sink and cabinet housing the drain pipe within the affected unit, creating sufficient working space for the rescue. Another team of rescuers proceeded to the unit directly below and cut a segment of the drain pipe. This allowed the rescuers to see how the arm was trapped and decide how to carefully manoeuvre the arm to free it. A lubricant was used to ease the arm out of the drain pipe. A medical team from Ng Teng Fong General Hospital was on-site to assess and render medical support to the person and had applied an intravenous drip. The person remained conscious throughout the rescue operation.The person was freed in about two hours from SCDFs arrival. SCDF conveyed the person to National University Hospital.

caption: [SCDF partners Tower Transit Singapore for the AED-on-Buses Programme]Yesterday (28 October), SCDF partnered with and to launch the AED-on-Buses Programme.Since the introduction of the AED-on-Wheels Programme in 2015, SCDF has collaborated with various organisations to enhance community access to Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) and strengthen the communitys capacity to respond to out-of-hospital cardiac arrests.This collaboration with Tower Transit marks the eighth partnership under the AED-on-Wheels programme, leveraging public transport, logistics and private-hire networks to augment SCDFs lifesaving mission.Under this partnership, buses serving industrial areas and neighbourhoods with a higher proportion of senior residents will be equipped with AEDs sponsored by the Singapore Heart Foundation. These AEDs can be used by commuters or Tower Transit Singapore Bus Captains, who have been trained in CPR and the use of AED under SCDFs Responders Plus Programme, to render immediate assistance to cardiac arrest victims before SCDFs arrival. The AED-on-Buses Programme underscores SCDFs commitment to building a resilient and prepared community, where every individual is empowered to act in times of need. Together, we continue to grow ANationofLifesavers and ensure that help is always within reach

caption: [Four heroes commended for saving the life of a cardiac arrest patient] On 13 September 2025 at about 8:00pm, a man suddenly collapsed at the badminton court of Block 108 Spottiswoode Park Road. Mr Sarar Khan, Mr Francan Chong, and Ms Tong Yao, who were in the vicinity, received a cardiac arrest incident alert via the SCDF myResponder app and immediately rushed to the scene. Mr Jason Poon, who was with Ms Tong at the time, also responded to the scene. Working as a team, the four individuals assessed the man and commenced CPR on him. One of the individuals also used an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) on the man to restore the mans heart rhythm. Through their teamwork and determination, the man is alive today. For saving a life, the four individuals were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award at the Bishan-Toa Payoh and Marymount Community Resilience Day. 16 other recipients across 13 separate incidents were also presented with the SCDF Community First Responder or Community Lifesaver Awards. The awards were presented by Mr Chee Hong Tat, Minister for National Development and Adviser for Bishan-Toa Payoh and Marymount Grassroots Organisations. In attendance at the presentation were Mr Cai Yinzhou and Ms Elysa Chen Shiyun, Advisers for Bishan-Toa Payoh and Marymount Grassroots Organisations, and COL Tay Zhi Wei, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Join us as a Community First Responder today by downloading and signing up via the myResponder app at go.gov.sg/myresponder today! caption: [Launch of the Better Awareness, Safer Homes campaign] Earlier today, the Bishan-Toa Payoh and Marymount Community Resilience Day was held. Mr Chee Hong Tat, Minister for National Development and Adviser for Bishan-Toa Payoh and Marymount Grassroots Organisations, attended the event as the Guest of Honour. The Community Resilience Day brings together residents and community leaders to share knowledge and pick up skills on fire safety and emergency preparedness, through informative booths, hands-on activities and live demonstrations. During the event, the Better Awareness, Safer Homes (BASH) campaign was also launched. This joint initiative by National Fire And Emergency Preparedness Council - NFEC, SCDF and Peoples Association aims to enhance fire safety awareness and encourage residents and the community to take ownership of fire safety within homes and in common public spaces. As part of the nation-wide BASH campaign efforts, NFEC has shared an updated Fire Safety Checklist and conducted training for Community Emergency and Engagement Committees (C2Es) and Town Councils representatives. C2Es will also step up block surveys of common areas to identify HDB estate facilities requiring maintenance via the OneService app. SCDF will continue to work closely with our partners and the community to enhance fire safety in Singapore. Remember, fire safety is our collective responsibility!

caption: [Fire @ Blk 68 Redhill Close]Earlier this morning at about 1:15am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, the living room of a fourth-floor unit was on fire. SCDF extinguished the fire with a water jet. The fire was confined to the living room.Firefighters rescued three persons from one of the bedrooms. They were conscious and assessed for smoke inhalation and minor burn injuries. The three persons were conveyed to Singapore General Hospital (SGH). Another person from a unit on a different floor felt unwell and was also conveyed to SGH.About 50 persons from the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure.Preliminary findings indicate that the cause of the fire is likely from an electrical origin in the living room. To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public:a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires or cracked cords should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use only appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. SCDF conducted forcible entry into the unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet. The fire was confined to the living room. During the firefighting operation, firefighters rescued a person from the kitchen. The person was assessed for smoke inhalation and minor burn injuries, and conveyed conscious to Singapore General Hospital (SGH). caption: [ASEAN Strategic Policy Dialogue on Disaster Management 2025]Yesterday (20 August), the ASEAN Strategic Policy Dialogue on Disaster Management (SPDDM) 2025 took place at the Grand Hyatt Singapore.Jointly organised by the SCDF, ASEAN Secretariat, and the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre), with support from the European Union Support to AHA Centre (EU-SAHA), the SPDDM is held annually as a platform to drive thought leadership and chart strategic directions for the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM).This years theme, Building a Resilient Future: Advancing ASEANs Post-2025 Vision for Disaster Management, highlighted the importance of technology, policymaking, and adaptability in strengthening resilience against emerging disaster challenges. caption: [Fire @ Block 34 Jalan Bahagia]Yesterday night (9 Aug) at about 9:30pm, SCDF responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms in a unit on the 6th floor was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. There was no one inside the unit when SCDF arrived. About 50 persons from the affected block were evacuated by the SCDF and Police as a precaution. There were no reported injuries. Preliminary findings indicate that the cause of the fire is likely from an electrical origin in the affected bedroom.To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public:a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires or cracked cords should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use only appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time, or leave it charging overnight.
